q6.answer: Order drives the checkout: it calls Inventory to reserve, moves itself between states on events (StockReserved out, PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined in), and calls claim/release. The record of progress is the order status in Order's own database (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID, etc.), with an Order sweeper restarting stuck PENDING or PAID orders. There is no separate orchestrator or saga table; it is event choreography plus Order's status.

q7.answer: Provider calls a webhook on Payment. Payment records it in one transaction (dedupe insert, PENDING to SUCCEEDED/DECLINED, outbox row), and the relay publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker. Order consumes it and finishes the order. A 35-minute Payment poller asks the provider directly if no webhook arrives.

q8.answer: Two layers. Payment stores the provider event id under a unique constraint, so a repeat webhook gets 200 and nothing happens. A payment also leaves PENDING only once via a conditional update, so poller and webhook cannot both publish. On the Order side every transition is a conditional update, so a duplicate event changes nothing and sends no event or email.

q9.answer: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined. Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED (only if still AWAITING_PAYMENT) and, only if that update changed the order, sends Inventory an HTTP release. Release turns an ACTIVE reservation into RELEASED and stock goes back on sale; other states are a no-op. Order retries the release until ok, and the 10-minute expiry frees the stock anyway.

q10.answer: When PaymentSucceeded arrives, Order saves PAID and calls claim. Inventory checks the reservation: if the hold lapsed (EXPIRED) but all lines are still free, it re-takes them and the order is fulfilled; if any line has been sold, the claim fails and Order cancels as CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and requests a full refund. I chose to fulfil when stock is still free rather than always refund; the brief did not specify this, and it is flagged as a decision the user may change.

q11.answer: Payment keeps a refund record REFUND_PENDING (unique per order id) with an attempt count and next-retry time in its own database. A refund retrier timer re-sends the request with idempotency key refund+order id, with backoff. At the retry limit the record becomes REFUND_FAILED, alerts on-call, goes to a manual queue, and is still retried slowly. The nature of the manual queue and what closing it does are not decided.

q12.answer: Order's OrderConfirmed event, published when the order becomes CONFIRMED, causes it. Cart consumes it and removes exactly the ordered lines and quantities from that cart (not the whole cart), recording the order id in a handled-order table in the same transaction so a repeat does nothing. Cart is the service that does it. This narrows the brief's 'emptied' and is flagged as changeable.
